summary: Streaming disconnects behind enterprise proxy; SDK retry guidance + better error surfaces needed (request_id, partial output)
description:
Issue summary:
Acorn Financial reports frequent disconnects when using streaming responses from Redwood (SSE) from within their corporate network. They are behind an enterprise HTTP proxy (Zscaler-like) and observe the stream terminating mid-response (partial output) with different error messages depending on SDK/language. They request explicit guidance on safe retry behavior for streaming and want request_id surfaced consistently for triage.

Impact:
- Production feature degraded: customers see truncated model outputs or UI hangs when stream ends unexpectedly.
- Retries are currently ad-hoc; customer concerned about duplicate side effects / duplicate billing when reissuing requests.
- Support unable to quickly correlate failures because request_id is not always present in SDK exceptions for streaming disconnects.

Environment:
- Customer tier: enterprise
- Region: us-east
- Network: corporate outbound proxy with TLS interception and idle connection policy
- Observed in: TypeScript SDK (Node 18), Python SDK (3.11), Go SDK (1.21)
- Endpoint: /v1/chat.completions with stream=true (SSE)

Customer-reported behavior:
- Stream runs for ~10–40 seconds then disconnects (no explicit error from API); client receives one of:
  - Node: "TypeError: fetch failed" / "ECONNRESET" or "socket hang up"
  - Python: "httpx.ReadError: [Errno 104] Connection reset by peer" or "RemoteProtocolError: Server disconnected"
  - Go: "unexpected EOF" while reading event stream
- Partial text is sometimes available in the UI, but the SDK throws and caller is unsure whether to display partial output or treat as failure.
- Customer notes that non-streaming requests are more reliable (but latency is worse).

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Route outbound traffic through corporate proxy (CONNECT).
2) Run streaming chat completion with longer responses (max_tokens >= 800) and low temperature.
3) Observe intermittent disconnects; rate increases during peak proxy load.

Evidence/log snippets (redacted):
- Customer TS log:
  - "stream error: ECONNRESET" after receiving ~1200 chars; no request_id available in the exception.
- Customer Python log:
  - "httpx.RemoteProtocolError: Server disconnected"; request_id not printed.
- Customer captured response headers from successful calls show x-request-id present, but failures do not surface it.

Initial hypothesis:
- Proxy closes idle/long-lived connections or buffers SSE chunks; may terminate mid-chunk causing client-side protocol errors.
- SDK streaming implementations differ in how they parse SSE and how they attach request_id to raised errors.

What we need:
1) Clear docs guidance for streaming disconnects behind proxies (recommended timeouts, keepalive, proxy settings, partial output handling).
2) SDK behavior: on streaming disconnect, raise typed error containing request_id (if known), status_code if available, and include partial_output (or guidance on how to capture it).
3) Conservative retry guidance (streaming retries should not be automatic; document idempotency keys + request_id logging).

Success criteria:
- Customer can log request_id and provide it to Support for any failure.
- Docs provide recommended patterns: retry policy for non-streaming vs streaming; show safe resume/retry patterns.
- SDKs align on an error taxonomy so customers see consistent fields across languages.
comments: 2026-01-29 09:22 (Dev Patel): Ticket opened after CS escalation. Customer reports 5–15% of streamed responses end abruptly behind corporate proxy. Asking for guidance + request_id surfacing. Assigning to Owen for repro + coordination with SDK team.

2026-01-29 10:05 (Owen Phillips): Acknowledged. Requesting: (1) which proxy vendor/policy (idle timeout?), (2) whether they can bypass proxy to confirm correlation, (3) SDK versions + minimal repro, (4) confirm they can capture response headers for successful stream start (x-request-id).

2026-01-29 14:18 (Customer - Acorn Financial): Proxy is managed by IT; appears to terminate long-lived connections. Cannot fully bypass in prod, but can test in a separate network where issue disappears. SDK versions: TS 0.18.2, Python 0.14.7, Go 0.9.1. They can capture x-request-id on successful responses but failures throw before they can access it.

2026-01-30 09:02 (Owen Phillips): Repro attempt internally using a proxy simulator that cuts connections mid-chunk; observed similar errors: Node fetch fails with ECONNRESET; Python httpx raises RemoteProtocolError; Go returns unexpected EOF. Confirms we do not consistently attach request_id for streaming disconnects because headers are read at stream start but not retained/propagated in error path in some SDKs.

2026-01-30 10:21 (Allison Grant): From SRE perspective: do NOT auto-retry streaming by default. Encourage idempotency keys for non-streaming retries; for streaming, recommend application-level retry with explicit user confirmation or safe idempotent semantics. Also recommend exposing disconnect_reason and retry_count fields where possible for debugging.

2026-01-31 11:44 (Sabrina James): Python SDK: we can retain response headers at stream start and include request_id in any downstream stream iterator exception. Also can include a StreamingError that optionally carries partial_text collected so far (opt-in due to memory). Tracking under SDK parity work; will reference this ticket in PR.

2026-02-02 15:09 (Dana Lo): TS SDK: node fetch streaming loses access to headers after consumption in some paths; but we can capture request_id early and attach to a typed error when ReadableStream errors. Also clarifying cancellation semantics vs network disconnect in docs/examples.

2026-02-03 13:27 (Mateusz Zielinski): Go SDK: we can wrap scanner/decoder errors and include request_id captured from initial response. Will also document recommended retry pattern and that retries are caller-controlled for streams.

2026-02-05 09:40 (Owen Phillips): Sent interim workaround to customer:
- If possible, configure proxy to allow long-lived SSE and disable response buffering for the Redwood domain.
- Increase overall timeout and keep connection alive (TCP keepalive) where supported.
- For best reliability behind strict proxies, consider non-streaming mode for long outputs.
- For retries: avoid automatic retry on streaming disconnect; if retrying, log request_id and use idempotency keys for any side-effecting workflows; treat partial output as best-effort display only.
Customer acknowledged and will test proxy policy changes.

2026-02-07 16:12 (Owen Phillips): Internal: linked this issue to INT-1182 (request_id visibility in SDK errors). Also flagged as a concrete driver for SDK parity initiative (streaming edge cases + typed errors).

2026-02-10 12:33 (Wei Chen): Drafted doc updates for Streaming guide: new section "Behind proxies" + "What to do on disconnect" including sample code to log request_id and capture partial output. Will align wording across Python/TS/Go pages and add explicit warning that streaming retries are not automatic.

2026-02-14 10:50 (Owen Phillips): Engineering updates in flight:
- Python: add typed StreamingDisconnectError w/ request_id and partial output semantics.
- TS: attach request_id and normalize error shape on stream failure.
- Go: wrap unexpected EOF with typed error + request_id.
Docs + examples to include idempotency guidance and consistent logging fields.
Keeping ticket in progress until customer confirms improvements or docs are published.

2026-02-18 09:07 (Customer - Acorn Financial): Proxy team applied allowlist + disabled buffering for Redwood streaming endpoint; disconnect rate reduced significantly but not eliminated. They still want request_id in errors to speed up escalation and want clear guidance on when to retry.

2026-02-19 17:28 (Owen Phillips): Docs PR and SDK PRs merged/queued for release per parity rollout. Provided customer with preview link and recommended pattern:
- Always log request_id at stream start.
- On disconnect: show partial output (if acceptable) and present a "Regenerate" action rather than silent automatic retry.
- For background jobs: prefer non-streaming with idempotency key and standard retry policy.
Customer satisfied with plan; will upgrade SDKs when releases land.

2026-02-20 11:02 (Dev Patel): Closing as resolved via docs guidance + upcoming SDK changes (typed errors w/ request_id, clarified partial output + retry guidance). Follow-ups tracked in SDK parity epic and INT-1182. If customer sees ongoing high disconnect rate after proxy changes, we will re-open for deeper platform/proxy analysis.
resolution: Resolved via (1) published streaming docs guidance for enterprise proxies and safe retry patterns, and (2) SDK parity work to surface typed streaming disconnect errors including request_id and consistent semantics for partial output/cancellation. Customer implemented proxy allowlist/buffering changes as a mitigation and will upgrade SDKs to pick up improved error surfaces.
